analysis.title: Top Stories
key_insights: China's September industrial profits rose +14.4% y/y, up from +4.2% in August and the fastest pace since June. AI-related manufacturing offset persistently weak domestic demand.
South Korea's Q3 GDP grew +1% q/q annualized vs the Street's +0.8%, driven by AI-fueled chip exports and investment. Consumption contracted, which may complicate further interest-rate hikes.
The BoJ's underlying inflation gauge hit a three-year high. CPI excluding fresh food and special factors rose 3.2% y/y in September, up from 2.6% in August and well above the 2% target.

French consumer confidence fell to a 13-year low in October as households dealt with a bond selloff and violent protests. Respondents were more worried about finances, living standards and unemployment.
Flávio Bolsonaro dropped his challenge to Brazil's election result and his party conceded. Focus shifts to whether Lula will rein in spending as fiscal strains mount.
China is sending special envoys to the Middle East to help defuse tensions and prevent a resumption of US-Israeli strikes against Iran.
Private-equity firms are negotiating loan extensions on much of a $300 billion wall of debt that comes due starting in 2028. Rising interest rates have made refinancing more expensive this year.
The US and Canada are working on a deal to ease US tariffs on Canadian steel and autos, after trade talks broke down in August.
Israelis are voting in their first election since the 2023 Hamas attack. Netanyahu faces a razor-thin race against an opposition led by Gadi Eisenkot.

Hedge fund gross leverage was 312% (96th percentile over five years) while fundamental net leverage fell to 47%, a new one-year low. Investors have turned more defensive without fully cutting gross exposure, which GS PB says helps explain why the pain has been so persistent.
Many names report earnings today, both before and after the open. Pre-market includes SOFI, KO, BA, UPS, PYPL, FCX, RCL, SPGI and AMT. After the close includes V, HOOD, EQT, BKR, FFIV and WM.
US data today includes durable goods (est +1.9%, prior -0.1%), Conference Board consumer confidence (est 81, prior 81.9) and new home sales (est 650.5k, prior 684k).
